title: Reasoning router trigger rules as pure deterministic functions

test_cases.name: Purity and lack of side effects
test_cases.input_setup: Execute classify_clinical_complexity() 1,000 times with identical input
test_cases.expected_result: 1,000 identical classifications returned; zero state mutation
test_cases.evidence: Pure function verified: 1,000 executions yielded bitwise identical classifications

test_cases.name: Complex presentation escalation to complex tier
test_cases.input_setup: Evaluate clinical note matching 3 criteria (fillers, companion, differential)
test_cases.evidence: Complex escalation verified: 3 rules triggered -> tier=complex (deployment: gpt-5.6-sol)

test_cases.name: Simple presentation routes to simple tier
test_cases.expected_result: Classifies as tier='simple' with sub-millisecond execution
test_cases.evidence: Simple presentation routes to default tier=simple (deployment: gpt-5.6-luna)

test_cases.name: Deterministic decision mapping
test_cases.input_setup: Generate two decisions with identical text using evaluate_routing_rules

test_cases.name: Empty input safe default
test_cases.expected_result: Defaults gracefully to baseline tier; zero unhandled exceptions
test_cases.evidence: Empty text input handled safely: score=0, tier='simple'
